name: YouTube Publisher
description: Upload videos, including English landscape documentaries, as private YouTube drafts for manual review and publication in YouTube Studio; account, size, duration, and timeout limits apply

required_variables.description: Google OAuth2 client ID (from Google Cloud Console)
YouTube OAuth2 refresh token (obtained via initial consent flow)

skill.name: youtube_publish
skill.description: Upload private YouTube drafts for user review, including English landscape documentaries; no automatic public publication or guaranteed upload recovery
skill.system_prompt:
You have access to YouTube upload tools. All uploads are ALWAYS private drafts. Never publish automatically; the user reviews the private draft and manually publishes from YouTube Studio.

ACCOUNT SETUP: use a named YouTube Connection for the intended channel, bound through the agent's connections map or a structured skills entry with a per-skill connections override. agent_create and agent_update support these bindings in the updated code; runtime MCP agent configuration is a separate post-deployment step. Do not configure agents or upload merely to validate documentation. Keep credentials out of prompts and documentation. Call refresh_youtube_token before an authorized upload and pass its fresh access_token to upload_to_youtube.

ENGLISH DOCUMENTARIES: use a landscape master (for example 16:9), explicitly pass is_short:false and category_id:'27' (Education). Write an English title (at most 100 characters) and English description containing the synopsis, actual sources and credits, and an accurate disclosure of AI-generated or dramatized reconstructions. Do not present reconstructed scenes as archival footage. Do not invent sources. The tool does not set language or altered-content disclosure fields; the user must review the relevant settings in YouTube Studio.

SHORTS CAVEAT: is_short only controls automatic #Shorts addition and the returned URL, not YouTube categorization. true adds #Shorts if missing and returns /shorts/<id>; false skips adding the hashtag and returns /watch?v=<id>, but does not remove an existing hashtag or prevent Shorts classification. If omitted, the CURRENT LEGACY ffprobe detector uses positive width and height, height >= width, and 0 < duration <= 60.5 seconds; missing ffprobe or invalid probe values default to false. This has NOT been updated to YouTube's current square-or-vertical, up-to-3-minute Shorts rules. YouTube determines the actual category; neither hashtags nor URL shape override it.

LIMITS: verify the intended channel is enabled for uploads longer than 15 minutes. YouTube's maximum is 256 GB or 12 hours, whichever is less. Account restrictions, quota, rights checks, and processing can still prevent success. video_url accepts a server-local file path or an HTTPS download URL. AT's browser files API caps the entire multipart request at 256 MiB (268435456 bytes), so usable file size is slightly smaller. A server-local upload does not pass through that endpoint and has no same 256 MiB cap; disk space, copying, network, deadlines, and YouTube limits still apply.

TIMEOUTS AND RECOVERY: the outer agent tool_timeout (seconds), task deadlines, and cancellation can stop the entire operation before curl's own timeout. Allow for file staging, session initiation, and upload when configuring runtime later. Download curl uses --max-time 1800 and --retry 3; session initiation uses --max-time 60 and --retry 3; the video PUT uses --max-time 14400 (4 hours) without retries. These are request-level settings, not a whole-operation guarantee. The resumable session endpoint is used, but the handler does not persist sessions, query received offsets, or resume an interrupted transfer. It does not guarantee recovery from EOF, timeout, or account-limit errors.

If an upload times out or the outcome is unknown, stop and have the user check the intended channel in YouTube Studio for a private draft or processing video BEFORE retrying, to avoid duplicate uploads. Report a returned video ID and private URL without claiming processing or review is complete. Recommend user review of playback, English metadata, sources, reconstruction disclosure, rights, audience settings, and privacy before manual publication.

tools.name: refresh_youtube_token
tools.description: Refresh the YouTube OAuth2 access token using credentials resolved from the bound named YouTube Connection (or global variable fallback). Confirm the intended channel binding before uploading; keep the returned token secret.

tools.name: upload_to_youtube
tools.description: Upload a server-local video or HTTPS source as a PRIVATE draft for manual YouTube Studio review. Refresh the token first. For English landscape documentaries pass is_short:false, category_id:'27', and English metadata with sources and reconstruction disclosure. is_short controls hashtag addition and returned URL only, NOT YouTube categorization; the legacy detector is height >= width and 0 < duration <= 60.5s, not current square/vertical <=3min Shorts rules. Verify channel eligibility over 15min; YouTube maximum is 256 GB or 12h, whichever is less. Outer tool timeout applies; a 4h curl PUT and resumable session endpoint do not guarantee retries or interrupted-upload recovery. If outcome is unknown, check the channel before retrying to avoid duplicates. No automatic publication.

video_url.description: Path to the video file (local path like /tmp/at-compose-XXX/video.mp4) or HTTPS URL to download

description.description: Video description. For Shorts, #Shorts is auto-added; for long-form videos, do NOT include #Shorts.

category_id.description: YouTube category ID. Common values: 22 (People & Blogs, default), 24 (Entertainment), 28 (Science & Tech), 10 (Music), 27 (Education).

is_short.description: Optional. true = upload as YouTube Short (adds #Shorts, returns /shorts/ URL). false = long-form video (no #Shorts, returns /watch?v= URL). If omitted, the tool auto-detects via ffprobe (vertical AND ≤60s = Short).

tools.handler:
#!/bin/bash
set -e

ACCESS_TOKEN="$ARG_ACCESS_TOKEN"
VIDEO_URL="$ARG_VIDEO_URL"
VISIBILITY="private"
CATEGORY_ID="${ARG_CATEGORY_ID:-22}"
IS_SHORT_ARG="$ARG_IS_SHORT"

if [ -z "$ACCESS_TOKEN" ] || [ -z "$VIDEO_URL" ] || [ -z "$ARG_TITLE" ]; then
  echo '{"error": "Missing required parameters: access_token, video_url, and title are required"}'
  exit 0
fi

# Create temp directory
WORKDIR="${AT_WORK_DIR:-/tmp}/at-youtube-$(python3 -c 'import uuid; print(uuid.uuid4().hex[:10])')"
mkdir -p "$WORKDIR"
VIDEO_FILE="$WORKDIR/video.mp4"

# Get video file — handle local paths and URLs
if [ -f "$VIDEO_URL" ]; then
  cp "$VIDEO_URL" "$VIDEO_FILE"
elif echo "$VIDEO_URL" | grep -q '^file://'; then
  LOCAL_PATH=$(echo "$VIDEO_URL" | sed 's|^file://||')
  cp "$LOCAL_PATH" "$VIDEO_FILE"
elif echo "$VIDEO_URL" | grep -q '^/'; then
  cp "$VIDEO_URL" "$VIDEO_FILE"
else
  curl -sL --retry 3 --retry-delay 5 --connect-timeout 30 --max-time 1800 -o "$VIDEO_FILE" "$VIDEO_URL"
fi

if [ ! -f "$VIDEO_FILE" ] || [ ! -s "$VIDEO_FILE" ]; then
  echo '{"error": "Failed to get video file"}'
  rm -rf "$WORKDIR"
  exit 0
fi

VIDEO_SIZE=$(stat -c%s "$VIDEO_FILE" 2>/dev/null || stat -f%z "$VIDEO_FILE" 2>/dev/null || echo 0)

# Determine Short vs long-form.
# Auto-detect (vertical AND <=60s) only when is_short not explicitly set.
# Defaults to long-form (safer — avoids accidental Shorts classification on long videos).
IS_SHORT="false"
if [ "$IS_SHORT_ARG" = "true" ] || [ "$IS_SHORT_ARG" = "1" ] || [ "$IS_SHORT_ARG" = "yes" ]; then
  IS_SHORT="true"
elif [ "$IS_SHORT_ARG" = "false" ] || [ "$IS_SHORT_ARG" = "0" ] || [ "$IS_SHORT_ARG" = "no" ]; then
  IS_SHORT="false"
elif command -v ffprobe >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  W=$(ffprobe -v error -select_streams v:0 -show_entries stream=width  -of csv=p=0 "$VIDEO_FILE" 2>/dev/null | head -n1 | tr -d '\r')
  H=$(ffprobe -v error -select_streams v:0 -show_entries stream=height -of csv=p=0 "$VIDEO_FILE" 2>/dev/null | head -n1 | tr -d '\r')
  D=$(ffprobe -v error -show_entries format=duration -of csv=p=0 "$VIDEO_FILE" 2>/dev/null | head -n1 | tr -d '\r')
  IS_SHORT=$(W="$W" H="$H" D="$D" python3 -c "
import os
try:
    w=int(float(os.environ.get('W') or 0))
    h=int(float(os.environ.get('H') or 0))
    d=float(os.environ.get('D') or 0)
    print('true' if (h>0 and w>0 and h>=w and 0<d<=60.5) else 'false')
except Exception:
    print('false')
")
fi

# Build metadata JSON safely using python3 (avoids shell escaping issues)
METADATA=$(IS_SHORT="$IS_SHORT" python3 << 'PYEOF' - "$ARG_TITLE" "$ARG_DESCRIPTION" "${ARG_TAGS:-[]}" "$VISIBILITY" "$CATEGORY_ID"
import sys, json, os, re

title = sys.argv[1]
description = sys.argv[2]
tags_raw = sys.argv[3]
visibility = sys.argv[4]
category_id = sys.argv[5]
is_short = os.environ.get('IS_SHORT', 'false') == 'true'

# Parse tags
try:
    tags = json.loads(tags_raw)
    if not isinstance(tags, list):
        tags = []
except (json.JSONDecodeError, TypeError):
    tags = []

# Strip any system-reminder tags that may have leaked in
title = re.sub(r'<system-reminder>.*?</system-reminder>', '', title, flags=re.DOTALL).strip()
description = re.sub(r'<system-reminder>.*?</system-reminder>', '', description, flags=re.DOTALL).strip()

# Add #Shorts ONLY for shorts; long-form must NOT have it (otherwise YouTube may misclassify)
if is_short and "#Shorts" not in description:
    description += "\n\n#Shorts"

metadata = {
    "snippet": {
        "title": title[:100],
        "description": description,
        "tags": [str(t) for t in tags][:30],
        "categoryId": category_id
    },
    "status": {
        "privacyStatus": visibility,
        "selfDeclaredMadeForKids": False
    }
}

print(json.dumps(metadata))
PYEOF
)

if [ -z "$METADATA" ]; then
  echo '{"error": "Failed to build video metadata"}'
  rm -rf "$WORKDIR"
  exit 0
fi

# Step 1: Initiate resumable upload (small request, short timeout, retried)
UPLOAD_URL=$(curl -s -D - -o "$WORKDIR/init_body.txt" -X POST \
  --connect-timeout 30 --max-time 60 --retry 3 --retry-delay 5 \
  "https://www.googleapis.com/upload/youtube/v3/videos?uploadType=resumable&part=snippet,status" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ACCESS_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "X-Upload-Content-Type: video/mp4" \
  -H "X-Upload-Content-Length: $VIDEO_SIZE" \
  -d "$METADATA" | grep -i 'location:' | sed 's/[Ll]ocation: //;s/\r//')

if [ -z "$UPLOAD_URL" ]; then
  INIT_BODY=$(cat "$WORKDIR/init_body.txt" 2>/dev/null || echo 'unknown')
  echo "{\"error\": \"Failed to initiate upload\", \"details\": $(python3 -c "import json,sys; print(json.dumps(sys.stdin.read()))" <<< "$INIT_BODY")}"
  rm -rf "$WORKDIR"
  exit 0
fi

# Step 2: Upload the video — long timeouts for big files; -T streams the file (better than --data-binary for huge files)
UPLOAD_RESP=$(curl -s -w "\n%{http_code}" -X PUT "$UPLOAD_URL" \
  --connect-timeout 60 --max-time 14400 \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ACCESS_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: video/mp4" \
  -T "$VIDEO_FILE")

HTTP_CODE=$(echo "$UPLOAD_RESP" | tail -1)
RESP_BODY=$(echo "$UPLOAD_RESP" | sed '$d')

rm -rf "$WORKDIR"

if [ "$HTTP_CODE" = "200" ] || [ "$HTTP_CODE" = "201" ]; then
  VIDEO_ID=$(echo "$RESP_BODY" | python3 -c "import sys,json; print(json.load(sys.stdin).get('id',''))" 2>/dev/null || echo "")
  if [ "$IS_SHORT" = "true" ]; then
    VIDEO_URL_OUT="https://youtube.com/shorts/$VIDEO_ID"
  else
    VIDEO_URL_OUT="https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=$VIDEO_ID"
  fi
  echo "{\"video_id\": \"$VIDEO_ID\", \"status\": \"uploaded\", \"visibility\": \"$VISIBILITY\", \"is_short\": $IS_SHORT, \"url\": \"$VIDEO_URL_OUT\"}"
else
  echo "{\"error\": \"Upload failed (HTTP $HTTP_CODE)\", \"is_short\": $IS_SHORT, \"details\": $(python3 -c "import json,sys; print(json.dumps(sys.stdin.read()))" <<< "$RESP_BODY")}"
fi
